hints: Notice the diagram shows W, X, Y and Z all fully immersed with identical size and orientation at the same depth in water of density $\rho$.
Recall Archimedes principle that upthrust equals the weight of displaced fluid, $U = \rho V g$, which uses fluid density and displaced volume.
Compare the displaced volume $V$ for the four cuboids and decide whether object densities $4\rho$, $2\rho$, $\rho$ and $0.5\rho$ change that volume.
walkthrough: Identify what is the same: each cuboid has the same length, breadth and height and is fully immersed, so each displaces the same volume $V$ of water.
State the governing rule: by Archimedes principle, upthrust $U$ equals weight of displaced water, $U = \rho_{fluid} V_{displaced} g$.
Substitute the fluid values: here $\rho_{fluid} = \rho$ for water, so $U = \rho V g$ for every cuboid.

Check the role of $4\rho$, $2\rho$, $\rho$ and $0.5\rho$: these are densities of the solid materials, so they change weight $= \rho_{object}Vg$ and the force needed in the holding rod, but not $V_{displaced}$.
Conclude all four upthrusts are equal and non-zero, even for Y where object density equals water density. This is option A.

options.A: Upthrust equals weight of displaced water, and all four displace the same volume $V$ of water of density $\rho$, so $\rho Vg$ is identical.
options.B: Object density $4\rho$ versus $2\rho$ changes weight, not upthrust, because displaced water volume is the same.
options.C: Upthrust does not scale with object density, so X does not have twice the upthrust of W despite the density ratio.
options.D: Cuboid Y is fully surrounded by water at different depths top and bottom, so pressure difference still gives a non-zero upthrust $\rho Vg$.
